Question ID: MCR_U03_L01_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.DL.1

Which display best compares favorite lunch choices: pizza, salad, sandwich, or pasta?

feedback.text: Correct. A bar graph compares category frequencies clearly.
A histogram is for numerical intervals, not named categories.
A line graph is best for change over time, not category comparison.
A scatterplot compares two numerical variables, not one categorical variable.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U03_L01_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.DL.2

A bar graph shows 22 students chose bus and 15 chose car. What conclusion is supported?

feedback.text: The display compares two categories, but it does not say every student chose bus.

answer.text: More students chose bus than car.

feedback.text: Correct. The bar for bus is larger than the bar for car.

answer.text: Car is the most common choice.

feedback.text: Bus has the larger count, so car is not more common here.
The categories are transportation choices, not numerical heights.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U03_L01_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.DL.1

A teacher records quiz scores from 0 to 100 for 80 students. Which display best shows the distribution of scores by intervals?

feedback.text: A bar graph is mainly for separate categories.
A two-way table organizes two categorical variables, not score intervals.
Correct. A histogram groups numerical data into intervals.
A circle graph shows parts of a whole but not distribution shape as clearly.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U03_L01_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.DL.2

A line graph of cafeteria sales rises from Monday to Friday. What does the upward trend mean?

feedback.text: An upward trend means the values increased.
A line graph over weekdays shows change over time.
An upward trend does not mean the final value is zero.
Correct. A rising line over time shows an increase.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U03_L01_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.DL.1

Which data type is represented by shirt sizes small, medium, large, and extra large?

feedback.text: The values are labels, not measured numbers.
Correct. Shirt sizes are labels or categories.
There are not two numerical variables here.
The values are not recorded over time.
